Post ways to self improve in this thread.

  • Eating clean. 
Avoid processed foods, animal fats, sugar and too much dairy. As a general rule, if you feel "heavy" after eating a meal, the food probably was not that great for you. Clean out with Psyllium Husk and other colon cleansing, natural supplements. Your digestive system absorbs nutrients, so throwing a wrench in it's gears can make you tired and malnourished.
  • Keep a Journal
Keeping a journal is a great way to set goals and keep track of progress. Set a weekly goal, monthly goals and long term "dreams." Then decompose what needs to be done to see them through. For instance, if a 3 month goal was to make 1.2x bodyweight benchpress and my daily journal entries read "watched 1 season of breaking bad," then I would not be on track. However, if the first 3 days read "shuttled friend to hospital" then you're still on track, but ran into "life." One helpful tip for overcoming writers' block is to use text to speech on an android or iOS phone into a journaling app, or on your PC.
  • There is no time like the present, overcoming analysis paralysis
The main reason why people procrastinate is a fear of failure. Avoid procrastination by overcoming your fear of failure. Easier said than done right? Wrong! Ask yourself, "What do I need to do, that has to be perfect the first time, every time?" Unless you're a professional at russian roulette or sword swallowing, I'd say: Nothing. For instance, if you have an essay to write, you can overcome analysis paralysis by spilling all your thoughts out at once. This is also called "musing" or "Heuristics" because the act of typing helps you explore your thesis better. If it is organization or cleaning, just start with the nearest object to you and work from there. Soon, it will take an act of God to stop you from cleaning the whole house! If you are writing a program, then make your class header and start writing pseudo code, work out from there and then refine to the specifications of the project.
  • Mental Clarity
No-porn, No-fap, as unpleasant and almost humorous as it may seem, is actually a very important way to self improve. Fapping is a waste of time, drains your motivation, reduces your testosterone levels and creates an instant gratification feedback loop that obliterates your potential.
Make a goal, say, 1-week no fap. If you can go for a week, then try 2 weeks, if you relapse, then make a punishment that is self improving. For instance, "If I relapse, then I have to do 3 sets of 20 pushups!" Another way to help keep you from relapsing is to go to the gym. Shredding connective tissue is a great way to release endorphins and feel accomplishment without falling into fapping.
